title: Topic 1.1: Origin and Consequences of Sin

pages.lesson:
LESSON: ORIGIN AND CONSEQUENCES OF SIN

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: CREATION
Topic 1.1: Origin and Consequences of Sin

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Origin and Consequences of Sin. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why is it important to consider the consequences of something before acting?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain the origin of sin from the scriptures provided
2. identify moral values and life skills needed to overcome temptations
3. pray to God to overcome temptations in day-to-day life

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: ORIGIN AND CONSEQUENCES OF SIN
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Origin and Consequences of Sin helps you succeed in CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: ORIGIN AND CONSEQUENCES OF SIN
Study Origin and Consequences of Sin like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Explain the origin of sin from the scriptures provided

What this means
In this part you learn to explain the origin of sin from the scriptures provided. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain the origin of sin from the scriptures provided.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Origin and Consequences of Sin” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain the origin of sin from the scriptures provided. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Identify moral values and life skills needed to overcome temptations

What this means
In this part you learn to identify moral values and life skills needed to overcome temptations. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify moral values and life skills needed to overcome temptations.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Origin and Consequences of Sin in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify moral values and life skills needed to overcome temptations. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Pray to God to overcome temptations in day-to-day life

What this means
In this part you learn to pray to God to overcome temptations in day-to-day life. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: pray to God to overcome temptations in day-to-day life.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can pray to God to overcome temptations in day-to-day life. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Origin and Consequences of Sin is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Origin and Consequences of Sin” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: explain the origin of sin from the scriptures provided)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Origin and Consequences of Sin in your own words. (skill: identify moral values and life skills needed to overcome temptations)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: pray to God to overcome temptations in day-to-day life)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Origin and Consequences of Sin to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain the origin of sin from the scriptures provided.
3. Practise this skill: identify moral values and life skills needed to overcome temptations.
4. Practise this skill: pray to God to overcome temptations in day-to-day life.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Origin and Consequences of Sin from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Origin and Consequences of Sin: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Origin and Consequences of Sin?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is it important to consider the consequences of something before acting?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Origin and Consequences of Sin means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain the origin of sin from the scriptures provided.
5. Be able to: identify moral values and life skills needed to overcome temptations.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
